name: Total Autosomal Monosomy Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Cytogenetic Diagnostic Criteria for Total Autosomal Monosomy Syndrome

criteria.description: Cytogenetic analysis demonstrating monosomy of an entire autosomal chromosome in all or majority of cells
Severe intrauterine and postnatal growth retardation
Presence of multiple congenital malformations affecting multiple organ systems
Neonatal or early infant death due to multisystem failure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cytogenetic confirmation of total autosomal monosomy plus at least two major clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made postnatally or postmortem due to lethality.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete monosomy of a single autosomal chromosome
searchTerms: loss of an entire autosomal chromosome

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple congenital malformations involving craniofacial dysmorphism
searchTerms: multiple birth defects with facial differences
birth defects affecting head and face shape
holes or defects in heart walls

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to pulmonary hypoplasia
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to lung underdevelopment
poor lung growth causing breathing problems
weak immune system with frequent infections
repeated infections due to immune deficiency
hormone problems including low thyroid function

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations due to neurodevelopmental impairment
searchTerms: mental health problems from brain development issues
psychiatric symptoms due to neurodevelopmental delay
behavioral problems linked to brain impairment

laboratory: Complete monosomy detected by karyotyping or chromosomal microarray
imaging: Ultrasound showing multiple organ malformations including cardiac and renal anomalies
MRI may reveal microcephaly and brain malformations
genetic: Loss of one entire autosomal chromosome in all or majority of analyzed cells
No known viable autosomal monosomy except mosaic or partial forms
other: Severe growth retardation evident clinically and by prenatal ultrasound

distinguishingFeatures: Partial rather than complete loss of an autosomal chromosome
Less severe phenotype with possible survival beyond infancy
Presence of an extra chromosome rather than monosomy
Distinctive clinical features such as characteristic facial dysmorphism

redFlags: Severe intrauterine growth retardation with multiple congenital anomalies
Cytogenetic confirmation of complete autosomal monosomy
Early neonatal death due to multisystem organ failure
references: Orphanet: Total Autosomal Monosomy Syndrome - ORPHA:98141
Recent reviews on chromosomal monosomy and congenital malformations
